title: Why is watch time declining?

concepts.name: Data quality & deduplication
concepts.blurb: Event logs double-count. Find and remove re-sent events before trusting any trend.

concepts.name: Mix shift (composition effects)
concepts.blurb: An average can fall because WHO is in it changed, not because anyone behaves differently.

concepts.name: Segmentation
concepts.blurb: Split by cohort, device, and experiment arm to see where the change actually lives.

concepts.name: Correlation vs. causation
concepts.blurb: Three things changed on the same day. Separate them before blaming one.

concepts.name: Executive communication
concepts.blurb: Turn the analysis into a decision: what happened, how sure you are, who acts next.

brief: Weekly watch time per active user is down about 21% when I compare the last four weeks (Aug 3–30) to the four weeks before (Jul 6–Aug 2). Sign-ups are actually up, which makes this more confusing. Leadership meets Thursday and wants to know whether this is a real engagement problem and which team should act. You have users, sessions, content, subscriptions, experiments, and marketing_campaigns. Dig in and send me your findings and a recommendation.

resources.title: Data dictionary
resources.content:
users — one row per account: user_id, signup_date, plan, region, age_band, acquisition_channel.
sessions — one row per play event received by the analytics pipeline: session_id, user_id, content_id, device (mobile/web/tv), app_version (mobile only), started_at (UTC), minutes_watched.
content — catalog: content_id, title, genre, is_original, release_date.
subscriptions — current plan and status per user: plan, is_trial, status, started_at, cancelled_at.
experiments — A/B assignments: user_id, experiment, arm, assigned_at.
marketing_campaigns — campaign_id, name, channel, start_date, end_date, target_segment.

resources.title: Metric definition: watch time per active user
resources.content: For a given week (Mon–Sun, UTC): total minutes_watched across all sessions, divided by the number of distinct users with at least one session that week. Dashboard source: sessions table, no filters.

resources.title: Release calendar (Jul–Aug)
resources.content:
Jul 14 — web player 3.8 (UI polish)
Jul 28 — TV app 2.4 (bug fixes)
Aug 3 — mobile app 5.3.0 ("stability and analytics improvements")
Aug 17 — web player 3.9 (accessibility)

truthModel_INTERNAL_DO_NOT_EXPOSE_TO_USE.summary: The -21.5% headline decline is three things that all started on Aug 3. (1) Measurement artifact: mobile app 5.2.0 re-sent ~34% of mobile play events (duplicate rows seconds apart, new session_id); 5.3.0 fixed it on Aug 3, so the BEFORE period was inflated. Deduplicating shrinks the decline to about -13.8%. (2) Mix shift: the 'Summer Free Month' paid_social campaign (Aug 3-30) added young, mobile-heavy trial users who watch ~47 min/week vs ~128 for existing users; they are ~15% of active users in weeks 5-8. Existing users in the experiment control arm are flat (-0.8%). (3) Small real product effect: experiment autoplay_next_v2 (existing users, from Aug 3) turned autoplay off for the treatment arm, cutting TV minutes per session from ~59 to ~49; existing treatment users are down ~10% while control is flat.

drivers.name: Duplicate mobile events before Aug 3
drivers.evidence: Rows with same user_id + content_id + device within 120s, all app_version 5.2.0, none after Aug 3 except chance collisions.

drivers.name: Campaign acquisition mix
drivers.evidence: paid_social users signed up Aug 3-30; far lower minutes per active user; existing control users flat.

drivers.name: autoplay_next_v2 treatment arm
drivers.evidence: Treatment vs control among existing users; effect concentrated on TV.

redHerrings: plan label casing (basic vs Basic) from a billing migration
truthModel_INTERNAL_DO_NOT_EXPOSE_TO_USE.acceptanceNote: A strong answer separates measurement artifact from behaviour change, quantifies each driver at least roughly, notices existing users are roughly flat, and recommends: fix the dashboard metric (dedupe / annotate), report engagement by acquisition cohort, and review autoplay_next_v2 before rollout. Well-supported alternative framings with caveats can still score high; this is not keyword matching.
